sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Criminal Petition Nos.10093 Of 2023
 & 10094 Of 2023
Common Order :

The present criminal petitions are filed by the petitioners under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., seeking to quash the proceedings in FIR No.932 of 2023, dated 16.09.2023 on the file of Police Station, Cyber Crimes.

1st petitioner in Criminal Petition No.10093 of 2023 is the son of the petitioners in Criminal Petition No.10094 of 2023 and the 2nd petitioner in Criminal Petition No.10093 of 2023 is his uncle and local guardian at USA.

2. In both these matters, this Court heard Sri Hemender Nath Reddy, learned senior counsel representing Smt.K.Hemalatha, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri E.Ganesh, learned Assistant Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 and Sri A.Venkatesh, learned Senior Counsel representing Sri Sinde Mohan Devidas, learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
3.

Crime in FIR No.932 of 2021, dated 16.09.2023 on the file of Police Station, Cyber Crimes was registered for the offences punishable under Section 420 of IPC and Sections 66-C and 66-D of Information Technology Act, 2000 basing on the complaint lodged by the 2nd respondent.

The allegations levelled in the complaint are that complainant's daughter Kum.Late Aishwarya Thatikonda, who was a Project Manager, used to stay at Dallas, USA along with Sreyas Reddy and Anusha Karasala in one premises.

On 06-05-2023 there was a mass shooting took place at Allen Premium Outlet Mall, Dallas, USA wherein the daughter of respondent No.2 died on the spot and Sreyas Reddy sustained severe injuries and was hospitalised.

The belongings of the complainant's daughter were seized by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, USA and intimated to complainant's family to collect the same or to give authorization to anyone to collect the same.
Complainant's family didn't respond to the same.

Accordingly, Sreyas Reddy Dadi, who is the complainant's daughter's friend and another person by name Nandikonda Kamalnabha Reddy, a resident of USA,
took the belongings of the complainant's daughter without any authorization given by complainant's family and also without giving any intimation to the complainant's family about taking of the belongings.

4. The Complainant alleged that Sreyas Reddy who knows the I Phone Passcode of Complainant's daughter mobile phone, has illegally accessed the same in collusion with other petitioners, deleted all the data stored like WhatsApp Chat, I-Cloud & important data in the mobile phone and he used all of complainant's personal credit cards and saving amounts from the complainant's daughter's accounts.
On persistent questioning by the complainant, Sreyas Reddy admitted his guilt and transferred Rs.2,41,629/-, Rs.2,43,369/- and Rs.1,62,174/- through the account of Kamalanabha Reddy.
Challenging the said crime, the petitioners filed the present criminal petitions seeking to quash the same insofar as they relate to the petitioners.

sentences.text:
The learned senior counsel for the petitioners contends that this is a classic example where the official machinery has been misused by the respondents by registering a false case, foisted against the petitioners for the offences under Section 420 of IPC and Sections 66-C and 66-D of IT Act,
2000 with ulterior motives of harassing and defaming the petitioners with concocted facts and bald allegations.
He further contends that the entire issue revolves around the accident, which has been unfortunately taken place in USA, where the daughter of the de-facto complainant/2nd respondent has passed away.
He further submits that in the said shootout Sreyas Reddy Dadi/1st petitioner in Criminal Petition No.10093 of 2023 also sustained severe injuries and was hospitalised.

6. It is contended by learned senior counsel for the petitioners that when the de-facto complainant did not respond to the request of the FBI to collect the belongings of the deceased, the FBI authorities requested Kamalnabha Reddy/2nd petitioner in Criminal Petition No.10093 of 2023, to collect the belongings of the deceased.
Accordingly, said Kamalnabha Reddy collected and sent the same to India through the friends of the deceased.
The petitioners acted out of generosity and did not tamper with any of her belongings.
They did not access the phone of the deceased or deleted the data in it.
On 16.07.2023 the son of the de-facto complainant sent picture of the deceased "Splitwise" account to Kamalnabha Reddy and informed that Sreyas Reddy owed an amount of $8008.59.
Kamalnabha Reddy, believing that the said was the household expenses share of Sreyas Reddy to the deceased, transferred the said amount.
At the time of seeking repayment of the above said amount, the de-facto complainant did not make any allegation against the petitioners.
Sreyas Reddy is a victim of mass shooting, sustained three bullet wounds and is under recovery process with heavy medication and hence, his committing offence is a concocted fact.
Kamalnabha Reddy invested time, effort and monies to ensure speedy delivery of the mortal remains of the deceased to their family in India.

The complaint does not contain the dates of the alleged transfer of monies,
names of the banks, the date and place of transfers.
7.
It is further contended by the learned senior counsel for the petitioners that the complaint is bad for lack the ingredients of Section 420 of IPC or Sections 66-C and 66-D of IT Act, 2000.
The petitioners are self-sufficient and are earning hand sum income.

Sanction under Section 188 of Cr.P.C., from the Central Government, is required either to prosecute the petitioners or to investigate into the matter since the alleged incidents happened in USA and are investigated into in India.
Admittedly, no complaint was registered in USA about the present issue.

Sreyas Reddy and the daughter of the 2nd respondent are childhood friends and were residing along with one Anusha Kasarla in one premises by virtue of the lease agreement dated 20.05.2022 and there was no complaint prior to the alleged incident.

The present criminal proceedings are manifestly attended with mala-fide intention and are instituted maliciously with ulterior motive for coercing the petitioners to succumb to illegal demands and as a measure of arm-twists tactics.
Thus stating, the learned counsel for the petitioners prayed to allow the present criminal petitions by quashing the impugned criminal proceedings.

8. The learned counsel for the petitioners relied upon the decisions rendered in the cases of Mahamood Ali and others Vs.State of UP and others 1, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd, Vs.
N.R.Vairamani 2 and P.Ramdev, S/o.P.Deenvan Rao Vs. The State of Telangana 3.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned senior counsel Sri A.Venkatesh, appearing for the 2nd respondent/de-facto complainant, vehemently opposed the present criminal petitions mainly contending that due to the death of the deceased, the family members of the 2nd respondent were under deep grief and trauma and hence, they could not give authorization to anyone to receive the belongings of the deceased and subsequently, they came to know that Sreyas Reddy and Kamalnabha Reddy received the same without any authorization.

He further submits that after receipt of belongings, the 2nd respondent was astonished to know that the WhatsApp charts,
I-Cloud chat and important data from the mobile phone of the deceased were erased by Sreyas Reddy in collusion with other petitioners and illegally accessed into the bank accounts and credit cards of the deceased.

Upon persistent questioning, Sreyas Reddy admitted his guilt of 2023 SCC OnLine SC 950 (2004) 8 Supreme Court Cases 579 2023 0 Supreme (Telangana) 531 squeezing monies from the deceased and repaid Rs.2,41,629, Rs.2,43,369/- and Rs.1,62,174/- through the account of Kamalnabh Reddy.

sentences.text: He further contends that under Section 4 of IPC the Code shall apply to the offences committed by any Indian in any place without and beyond India and that since Sreyas Reddy continues to be a citizen of India and has not acquired citizenship of USA, there is no bar to prosecute him in India for the offences committed.

10. Learned senior counsel for the respondent No.2 relied upon the decisions rendered in Hukum Chand Garg and another Vs.State of Uttar Pradesh and others 4 and Thota Venkateswarlu Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh through the Principal Secretary and another 5 contending that the petitioners have not been made as accused in the FIR and hence, the question of quashing the FIR does not arise since the petitioners will have no locus to seek such relief.

sentences.text: He further contends that sanction under Section 188 of Cr.P.C., is not a condition precedent for taking cognizance of an offence and, if need be, it could be obtained before the trial begins.
Stating thus, he seeks to dismiss the present criminal petitions.
2022 SCC OnLine SC 2165 (2011) 9 Supreme Court Cases 527 11.

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor taking the same stand of learned counsel for the respondent No.2, would submit that the case is at the stage of investigation and without the petitioners being arrayed as accused in the FIR, they rushed to the Court.
He further submits that unless and until the investigation is concluded, the role of the petitioners cannot be decided.
Stating thus, he seeks to dismiss the present criminal petitions.
12. This Court heard the rival contentions advanced on behalf of the parties and perused the material on record.
It is an admitted fact that the petitioners have rushed to the Court in a premature manner without arraigning them as accused in the FIR.
The case is at the stage of investigation.
The matter requires detailed examination.

In view of the above, this Court directs the respondent/police to issue notice under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C. to the petitioners facilitating them to give explanation/reply to the same within fifteen days thereon.

The respondent/police are directed not to take any coercive steps against the petitioners, including their arrest, and to complete the investigation as quickly as possible strictly adhering to the law laid down and the guidelines stipulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar and another 6.
